title: Market Reactions to Material Cybersecurity Incidents
hypothesis: H1: companies filing a material cybersecurity incident (Item 1.05 8-K) experience a negative short-term stock reaction (mean event-window return <0). H1,2: Technology companies exhibit larger negative reactions than other sectors. H1,3: Smaller companies (<$2B) experience stronger negative reactions than larger companies. H1,4: Higher beta companies exhibit larger price drops than lower beta companies.
data_sources: SEC EDGAR database - Form 8-K filings including Item 1.05 Material Cybersecurity Incidents
sec-api Python library (10-K/10-Q/8-K Section Extractor API) for 8-K Item 1.05 metadata, ticker, CIK, filing timestamp
yfinance Python library using Yahoo public API for daily close stock prices and company metadata (sector, market capitalization, beta)
sample: Event is filing of Form 8-K Item 1.05 Material Cybersecurity Incident. Sample is all such filings submitted to SEC and available as of November 12th, 2025: 54 reports corresponding to 36 unique companies. No duplicate reports included; multiple incidents by same company on different dates treated as separate events. Filing trading day defined as filing date, or first trading day after if filing on non-trading day. Event window is previous market trading day before filing through five market trading days after (seven-day window). Filters: observations with missing price data, invalid market cap, missing beta or missing sector excluded from analyses requiring those variables (e.g., size comparison uses 24 small + 29 larger =53).
method: Collect all Form 8-K filings with Item 1.05 from SEC EDGAR via sec-api, retaining ticker, CIK and filing timestamp; final dataset as of November 12 2025.
Define filing trading day: if filing date is non-trading day, define filing date as first trading day after filing date.
For each event collect daily closing prices over seven-day window: from previous market open day before 8-K filing through five market days after filing date.
Compute market reaction as percentage return defined as change from closing price on trading day before filing to five trading days after.
Test overall effect with one-sample left-tailed t-test H0: mu=0 vs H1: mu<0.

Test subgroup effects with left-tailed Welch two-sample t-tests: Technology vs non-technology; Small (<$2B) vs all larger (Mid $2-10B + Large $10-200B + Mega >=$200B) combined; high vs low beta split at sample median beta.
Exclude from analyses requiring those variables observations with missing price data, invalid market capitalization values, missing beta data, or missing sector classifications.
